title: Tech Mahindra Q1 Profit Surges 28% as Deal Wins Top $1 Billion
excerpt: The Pune-based IT services firm posted revenue of ₹15,712 crore and its fourth consecutive quarter of margin expansion, while new deal wins rose 33% year-on-year.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Tech Mahindra's Q1 profit surged 28.4% to ₹1,465 crore, with revenue up 17.7% to ₹15,712 crore.
  • EBIT margin expanded to 14.4%, marking four consecutive quarters of improvement under CEO Mohit Joshi.
  • New deal wins reached $1.08 billion, a 33.3% increase year-on-year, continuing a billion-dollar streak.
  • Brokerages are divided on stock valuation, with HSBC rating it a Buy and Jefferies an Underperform.

  • Tech Mahindra's consolidated net profit rose 28.4% year-on-year to ₹1,465 crore in Q1 FY27, with revenue climbing 17.7% to ₹15,712 crore.
  • EBIT margin expanded 60 basis points sequentially to 14.4%, marking four straight quarters of margin improvement under CEO Mohit Joshi's turnaround plan.
  • New deal wins hit $1.08 billion — up 33.3% year-on-year — extending a three-quarter streak of billion-dollar-plus bookings.
  • Brokerages remain divided: HSBC rates the stock a Buy at ₹1,635, while Jefferies maintains Underperform at ₹1,260.

Tech Mahindra reported a 28.4% year-on-year jump in consolidated net profit to ₹1,465 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, according to its earnings release on July 16. Revenue from operations rose 17.7% to ₹15,712 crore, beating analyst estimates of ₹15,486 crore.

In dollar terms, Q1 FY27 revenue came in at $1,660 million — up 6.1% year-on-year and 2.2% sequentially. In constant currency terms, the growth was 6.6% annually and 2.6% quarter-on-quarter.

Shares responded positively, climbing as much as 2.54% to ₹1,548.70 on July 17, making Tech Mahindra one of the top gainers on the Nifty 50.

Margin Expansion Continues

The profitability story was arguably more striking than the headline profit number. EBIT rose 53.3% year-on-year and 8.6% sequentially to ₹2,264 crore. The EBIT margin expanded 60 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 14.4% — 330 basis points higher than the year-ago period — marking the fourth consecutive quarter of margin improvement.

EBITDA stood at ₹2,742.5 crore, up 41.7% year-on-year, according to Capital Market.

“We delivered a strong Q1 performance with broad-based growth, margin expansion, and disciplined working capital management, reflecting consistent execution and sustained business momentum.”

— Rohit Anand, Chief Financial Officer, Tech Mahindra

"The communications segment — historically Tech Mahindra's anchor business — accounted for 32.3% of revenue, growing 1.3% annually."

"The communications segment — historically Tech Mahindra's anchor business — accounted for 32.3% of revenue, growing 1.3% annually."

Management is targeting a 15% EBIT margin by the end of FY27, according to HSBC's post-results analysis. The current trajectory suggests that target is within reach.

Deal Pipeline Strengthens

New deal wins (total contract value) stood at $1.078 billion in Q1, up 33.3% year-on-year, extending Tech Mahindra's streak of quarterly deal wins above $1 billion to three consecutive quarters. On a last-twelve-months basis, deal wins have climbed sharply, underscoring broad-based demand for the company's offerings.

“YoY growth of 6.1% coupled with three consecutive quarters of deal wins exceeding $1 billion dollars underscores the resilience of our business and the growing relevance of our offerings.”

— Mohit Joshi, CEO and Managing Director, Tech Mahindra

Client relationships deepened, with the $50 million-plus client base expanding by seven accounts. Three new clients were added in the $10 million bracket and four in the $50 million-plus category, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

Vertical and Geographic Mix

Deal Wins on the Rise
›New deal wins totaled $1.08 billion.
›33.3% increase year-on-year.
›Three consecutive quarters of over $1 billion in deals.
›Seven new clients added in the $50 million-plus category.

All verticals delivered year-on-year growth. The communications segment — historically Tech Mahindra's anchor business — accounted for 32.3% of revenue, growing 1.3% annually. Manufacturing, BFSI, retail logistics, and healthcare all posted growth on both sequential and annual bases. The technology, media, and entertainment segment rose 3.4% year-on-year but dipped sequentially.

Geographically, Europe was the standout, growing 12.1% year-on-year and 8.1% sequentially. The Americas, which remains the largest market, rose 4.8% annually but was essentially flat quarter-on-quarter. The rest-of-world segment grew 2.5% sequentially.

Headcount and Attrition

Total headcount stood at 146,760, down by 863 employees quarter-on-quarter. IT headcount specifically was 74,689, down 688 sequentially. The company's last-twelve-month IT attrition rate held steady at 11.8%. Cash and cash equivalents stood at ₹9,695 crore, while days sales outstanding was 84 days.

Brokerages Split on Valuation

The operational beat drew praise from analysts, but views on the stock diverged sharply. HSBC maintained its Buy rating with a target price of ₹1,635, saying margin expansion remains on track and stronger growth than peers supports a premium valuation.

Nomura retained a Neutral rating at ₹1,600, noting the company is on track for its FY27 objectives but cautioning that the stock already trades at 17.1 times FY28 earnings. Jefferies kept its Underperform call at ₹1,260, raising FY27-FY29 earnings estimates by 6-8% but arguing that even a projected 4% revenue CAGR and 9% EPS CAGR over FY27-FY29 don't justify the current valuation, according to Outlook Business.

Despite the post-results rally, Tech Mahindra shares remain down 5.7% year-to-date in 2026, compared with a 7.9% decline in the broader Nifty 50.

Market Reactions and Analyst Views
›HSBC maintains Buy rating at ₹1,635.
›Jefferies rates Underperform at ₹1,260.
›Tech Mahindra shares down 5.7% year-to-date.
›Nifty 50 index down 7.9% year-to-date.

What's Next

With the turnaround under CEO Mohit Joshi now in its second year, the focus shifts to whether Tech Mahindra can sustain its margin expansion trajectory toward the 15% EBIT target while maintaining the current deal-win momentum. The company's investments in sovereign AI, domain-specific platforms, and digital capabilities will be key to converting its strengthening pipeline into durable revenue growth. Its next quarterly results are due in October 2026.
